solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dropping sadly can limit cacti in development (13)

indicators.note: something in development is still changing shape, so the letters are not yet in their final order

annotation.surface: A gardener watches a stunted cactus collection fail to thrive.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: an anticlimax is a let-down that comes just when things were building up.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: an anticlimactic moment is a disappointing drop after rising expectation.

clue.text: Where hands go through three consecutive eight-hour shifts? (6,3,5)

definitions.text: Where hands go through three consecutive eight-hour shifts?

blocks.note: the surface reads hands as workers clocking on; the setter means the pointers on a dial, and where they travel
three eight-hour shifts in a row make up a full 24 hours, the time those pointers take to go round twice

annotation.surface: A factory rota keeps the workforce busy day and night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hands' reads as workers on shifts, but clock hands literally travel around the clock, and a 24-hour rota runs around the clock.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom read literally: working around the clock means non-stop, and clock hands physically go around the clock.

clue.text: Tons persistently worry over nasal sound (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word turned over is upside down, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: to gnaw at is to worry persistently

annotation.surface: Someone frets about a whining noise from their own nose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Persistently worry' looks like NAG, but it is GNAW, which reversed gives the WANG you need.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a twang is the resonant, through-the-nose quality of some voices and accents.

clue.text: What could be sharp chintz raincoat child’s regularly taken out (6,4)

indicators.note: letters removed at regular intervals means every other one goes

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters of these three words, read in order

annotation.surface: A child's garish flowered raincoat has been taken out of the wardrobe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' means sour-tasting here, not stylish, so the definition is a cautious 'could be': citric acid is one sharp thing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: citric acid is what makes lemons taste sharp, so it is one thing that could be sharp.

clue.text: Foolishness and madness banishing son (7)

indicators.note: to banish is to send away, so the son is removed from the word

annotation.surface: A family drama in which a father's folly ends with his son thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition and the wordplay nearly mean the same thing, which makes 'and' a natural join.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: inanity is empty-headed silliness.

clue.text: Pure northern Gaelic must be translated (7)

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, and here the letters are turned into another word

annotation.surface: A purist insists that a Highland text be rendered faithfully into English.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Translated' is natural next to a language name, which hides its job of rearranging letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: angels stand for innocence, so angelic means pure.

clue.text: One securing rank (4)

blocks.note: someone who ties things fast, the -er agent noun of 'tie'
a row or level in a stepped arrangement

annotation.surface: Someone clinches a promotion to a higher grade.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is the made-up-looking 'one who ties'; crosswords lean on these -ER agent nouns.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a crossword-only agent noun, one who ties, and the ordinary word for a row or level.

clue.text: Star locked up by prison governor (9)

indicators.note: something locked up by another is held inside it, so the star sits within the prison

blocks.note: stella is Latin for star, and a name

annotation.surface: A celebrity is jailed on the orders of the man who runs the prison.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prison governor' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'prison' is CAN in the wordplay and 'governor' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind of governor: a castellan was the official in charge of a castle.

clue.text: Is Carmine gored getting involved in this? (9,5)

definitions.text: Is Carmine gored getting involved in this?

indicators.note: things that get involved become tangled, so the letters are mixed up

annotation.surface: A gangster called Carmine gets stabbed after mixing with the Mob.
annotation.walkthrough: Carmine is a stock mobster's name, and getting gored is what happens to someone who gets mixed up with the Mafia.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: a Carmine getting knifed is just the fate you would expect from involvement in the Mafia world.

clue.text: Illusory images of neutrino particles? (2,3)

blocks.note: a neutrino has zero charge, and zero is O
a part is a small piece, like a particle

annotation.surface: A physicist asks whether pictures of subatomic particles are real.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the loose leaps: neutral charge read as zero, then O, and particles read as parts.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: op art is abstract art whose patterns create optical illusions.

clue.text: Gross rage is out of order for assailant (9)

indicators.note: things out of order are not in the right sequence, so the letters must be rearranged

annotation.surface: A disapproving verdict on someone's violent temper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' reads as a British reproach, meaning unacceptable, rather than a signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the aggressor is the one who attacks first.

clue.text: Unimportant note, for instance, readable with a typo? (10)

indicators.note: a typo is one wrongly struck letter, so one letter of the word is swapped

blocks.note: readable = LEGIBLE, with its first E mistyped as I

annotation.surface: A throwaway remark that a scribbled memo is legible despite a slip of the keys.
annotation.walkthrough: The typo is the key step: LEGIBLE needs one letter changed, and the crossing letters tell you which.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something negligible is too slight to be worth considering.

clue.text: Letter of thanks after Beeb has abolished repeats (4)

indicators.note: abolishing repeats gets rid of every letter that appears a second time
one piece placed after another comes later in the answer, so TA follows

blocks.note: BEEB with its doubled letters removed leaves B and E once each

annotation.surface: A thank-you note to the BBC after it stops showing reruns.
annotation.walkthrough: The Beeb is a nickname for the BBC, and 'repeats' are reruns in the surface but repeated letters in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Excitedly waves health food recipes (10)

blocks.note: bran is a classic health food

annotation.surface: An enthusiast holds up a wholefood cookbook.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'health food recipes' as one phrase; it splits after 'food'.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to brandish something is to wave it about with a flourish.

clue.text: Scrap, a bit of thin muslin (7)

blocks.note: a scrap is a quarrel, a tiff
'any' = a bit of, as in 'have you any milk?'

annotation.surface: A seamstress offers a small offcut of fine fabric.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' wants to be a scrap of cloth, beside muslin; it is a fight.
annotation.definitionFit: An old dictionary sense: tiffany is a gauzy, thin muslin fabric.

clue.text: Forcibly move ornamental coat fastener on border (9)

blocks.note: a frog is a looped braid fastening on a coat
a march is a frontier or border region

annotation.surface: A tailor's instruction to shift a decorative button along the edge of a coat.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the fastener above the border.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to frogmarch someone is to force them along with their arms held.

clue.text: Italian composer writes music endlessly, flipping bad (7)

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are cut off
to flip something is to turn it over, so the word reads backwards

annotation.surface: A composer's tireless output is dismissed as awful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word qualifying 'bad', but it is the reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque composer.

clue.text: Gradually losing stone, say, cut by sculptor (7)

indicators.note: something cut by a blade has the blade inside it, so the sculptor goes into the middle

annotation.surface: A sculptor chisels a block down bit by bit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stone' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay: rock that is eroding is gradually losing stone, and 'say' on its own gives EG.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: erosion is rock worn away little by little.

clue.text: Dumplings — no small volume covered in butter (7)

indicators.note: something covered in a coating is wrapped by it, so the letters sit inside the butter

blocks.note: cc = cubic centimetre, a small volume

annotation.surface: A dieter orders dumplings but wants them without too much butter.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash makes the surface a menu instruction; GHI is a recognised spelling of ghee.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: gnocchi are small Italian dumplings of potato or semolina.

clue.text: Atonement not unknown in pirates’ home (7)

indicators.note: 'not unknown' means without the unknown, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: The Pirates of Penzance, Gilbert and Sullivan's opera; Penzance is a Cornish town
z = an unknown in algebra, removed

annotation.surface: Buccaneers find no forgiveness back at base.
annotation.walkthrough: Algebra's unknowns are X, Y and Z; here it has to be Z. 'Not unknown' also reads as a double negative, which hides the deletion.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: penance is punishment undertaken to make amends for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Delay Broadway’s opening of play around November (7)

indicators.note: one thing around another encloses it, so the prologue wraps the N

blocks.note: the American spelling of prologue, so Broadway's version
N = November in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A theatre postpones its New York premiere until the autumn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadway's opening' tempts you to take B; Broadway is only there to make the prologue American, PROLOG.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to prolong something is to drag it out, delaying its end.

clue.text: What’s used to catch birds in tree (4)

blocks.note: a sticky paste smeared on branches so perching birds are stuck

annotation.surface: A bird-catcher sets a trap up a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: Birdlime was spread on twigs so perching birds stuck fast, hence 'lime' as a trap.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: short for birdlime, the old sticky trap, and another name for the linden tree.

clue.text: Big and impenetrable loch I’m into, swimming (10)

indicators.note: things swimming move about freely, so the letters shift position

annotation.surface: A wild swimmer boasts about a vast, murky Scottish lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Big and impenetrable' could describe the loch itself, which hides that it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a monolith is a single massive block of stone, so monolithic means huge and seamless.

clue.text: Port city of Nova Scotia unfinished and not large (5)

indicators.note: a word left unfinished lacks its last letter
'not large' means without the L, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: Halifax is the capital of Nova Scotia

annotation.surface: A geography note about a Canadian harbour town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port city' reads as one phrase, but only 'Port' is the definition; 'city of Nova Scotia' is HALIFAX.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Haifa is a major port in northern Israel.

clue.text: Cross about book being forbidden (4)

indicators.note: one thing about another surrounds it, so the cross goes round the book

annotation.surface: Someone is angry that a book has been banned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the T-shaped tau cross. TABU is a variant spelling of taboo.
annotation.definitionFit: A variant spelling: tabu is taboo, the word for something banned by custom.

clue.text: Hors d’œuvre of fish I love after starters of artisanal cold cuts (9)

indicators.note: 'I love after' the initials means those two letters come later in the answer than the initials
the starters of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: first letters of Artisanal Cold Cuts

annotation.surface: A diner praises a starter of fish alongside a platter of craft charcuterie.
annotation.walkthrough: The cold cuts belong to the wordplay but also hint at the answer, which is thinly sliced raw meat or fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: carpaccio is a starter of thinly sliced raw beef or fish.

clue.text: West end of Hispaniola island — not all of it? (5)

definitions.text: West end of Hispaniola island — not all of it?

indicators.note: on a map west is the left, and the left end of a word is its first letter
not all of a word means it is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: the left-hand, western, letter of HISPANIOLA
an ait is a small river island

annotation.surface: A geography question about how the Caribbean island is divided.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Haiti occupies the western part of Hispaniola, not the entire island.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: Haiti takes up the western third of Hispaniola, sharing it with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Washing car outside university residential area (7,6)

indicators.note: one word outside another encloses it, so the washing goes round the university

blocks.note: an estate car is the British name for a station wagon

annotation.surface: Someone hoses down their car outside the student halls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Washing car' reads as one activity, and 'outside university' as a location; both split, with 'outside' telling the washing to wrap the university.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term: a housing estate is a planned development of homes built together.
